metadata.title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events to Their Probabilities
metadata.authors: V. N. Vapnik and A. Ya. Chervonenkis
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Probability space and sample space
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of elementary events with probability measure $P_X$, $S$ a collection of $P_X$-measurable subsets (events), and $X^{(l)}$ the space of size-$l$ samples in $X$ equipped with the product probability measure $P$.
nodes.statement_clean: Setup: a probability space $X$ with measure $P_X$, an event class $S$, and product samples of size $l$.

nodes.name: Relative frequency $\nu_A^{(l)}$
nodes.statement: For sample $x_1,\dots,x_l$ and event $A\in S$, the relative frequency is $\nu_A^{(l)} = n_A/l$, where $n_A$ is the number of sample elements lying in $A$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical frequency of $A$ in the sample.

nodes.name: Maximum deviation $\pi^{(l)}$
nodes.statement: $\pi^{(l)} = \sup_{A\in S} |\nu_A^{(l)} - P_A|$, the worst-case discrepancy between empirical frequency and probability over the class $S$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sup over $S$ of $|\text{empirical} - \text{true}|$.

nodes.name: Uniform convergence over $S$
nodes.statement: Relative frequencies converge uniformly (in probability) to probabilities over $S$ if $\lim_{l\to\infty} P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\} = 0$ for every $\epsilon > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of uniform convergence in probability of empirical to true measure.

nodes.name: Index $\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_r)$
nodes.statement: For a sample $X=x_1,\dots,x_r$, the index $\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ is the number of distinct subsamples induced on $X$ by sets of $S$. Always $\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_r) \le 2^r$.
nodes.statement_clean: Number of distinct intersection patterns of $S$ with the sample.

nodes.name: Growth function $m^S(r)$
nodes.statement: $m^S(r) = \max_{x_1,\dots,x_r} \Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_r)$, the maximum number of distinct subsamples that $S$ can induce on any sample of size $r$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum index over all samples of size $r$.

nodes.name: Function $\Phi(n,r)$
nodes.statement: $\Phi(n,r)$ is defined by the recurrence $\Phi(n,r) = \Phi(n,r-1) + \Phi(n-1,r-1)$ with $\Phi(0,r)=1$ and $\Phi(n,0)=1$. For $n>0$, $r\ge 0$, $\Phi(n,r) \le r^n + 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combinatorial recurrence used to bound the growth function.

nodes.name: Entropy $H^S(l)$ of the system $S$
nodes.section: 2.6 Some additional properties of the index
nodes.statement: $H^S(l) = E[\log_2 \Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_l)]$, the expected log-index over a random sample of size $l$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected log of number of induced subsamples.

nodes.name: Rays on the line
nodes.statement: Let $X=\mathbb{R}$ and $S = \{(-\infty, a] : a\in\mathbb{R}\}$. Then $m^S(r) = r+1$.
nodes.statement_clean: For half-line events, the growth function is linear in $r$.

nodes.name: All open subsets of $[0,1]$
nodes.statement: Let $X=[0,1]$ and $S$ the family of all open sets. Then $m^S(r) = 2^r$.
nodes.statement_clean: An overly rich class for which the growth function is maximal.

nodes.name: Half-spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$
nodes.statement: $X=\mathbb{R}^n$, $S = \{\{x : \langle x,\varphi\rangle \ge 1\} : \varphi\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$. Then $m^S(r) = \Phi(n,r)$, the maximum number of cells into which $r$ hyperplanes partition $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.statement_clean: For half-spaces, the growth function equals the hyperplane-arrangement count $\Phi(n,r)$.

nodes.name: Combinatorial dichotomy lemma (Lemma 1)
nodes.statement: If for some sample of size $i$ and $1 \le n \le i$, $\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_i) \ge \Phi(n,i)$, then there exists a subsample $x_{j_1},\dots,x_{j_n}$ of size $n$ with $\Delta^S(x_{j_1},\dots,x_{j_n}) = 2^n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Index above $\Phi(n,i)$ forces a shattered subsample of size $n$.
conclusions: There exists a size-$n$ subsample with $\Delta^S = 2^n$ (a shattered set)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Induction on the sample size; case-split subsamples by whether both extensions $t$ and $t\cup\{x_i\}$ are induced, then use the recurrence for $\Phi(n,r)$ to derive a contradiction.

nodes.name: Set up induction and base/edge cases
nodes.statement: Verify the lemma directly for $n=1$ and for $n=i$ (using $\Phi(1,i)\ge 2$ and $\Phi(i,i)=2^i$). Assume by induction that the lemma holds for all smaller $i$ and all $n<i$.

nodes.name: Split subsamples into two types
nodes.statement: For sample $X_{r-1}$, partition the induced subsamples into type-1 (only one of $t$, $t\cup\{x_r\}$ induced on $X_r$) and type-2 (both induced), with counts $a$ and $b$. Then $\Delta^S(X_{r-1}) = a+b$ and $\Delta^S(X_r) = a+2b$.

nodes.name: Bound $b$ via the inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: If some size-$(n-1)$ subsample of $X_{r-1}$ had $\Delta^{S''} = 2^{n-1}$, augmenting it with $x_r$ would give a shattered $n$-set in $X_r$, contradicting the assumption. Hence $b \le \Phi(n-1, r-1)$.

nodes.name: Combine using the recurrence to reach a contradiction
nodes.statement: Substituting yields $\Delta^S(X_r) \le \Phi(n, r-1) + \Phi(n-1, r-1) = \Phi(n,r)$, contradicting $\Delta^S(X_r) \ge \Phi(n,r)$. The lemma is proved.

nodes.name: Growth-function dichotomy (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: The growth function $m^S(r)$ is either identically equal to $2^r$ or majorized by $r^n + 1$, where $n$ is the smallest $r$ for which $m^S(r) = 2^r$ fails.
nodes.statement_clean: Either $S$ shatters arbitrarily large samples, or $m^S$ grows polynomially with exponent equal to the VC-dimension.
conclusions: Either $m^S(r) \equiv 2^r$, or $m^S(r) \le r^n + 1$ where $n$ is the first $r$ with $m^S(r) < 2^r$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: If $m^S(r) < 2^r$ for some $r$ with smallest such value $n$, apply Lemma 1 contrapositively: $\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_r) \ge \Phi(n,r)$ would yield a shattered $n$-subsample, contradicting $m^S(n)<2^n$. Hence $m^S(r)<\Phi(n,r)\le r^n + 1$.

nodes.name: Two-sample deviation $\rho^{(l)}$
nodes.statement:
For a sample of size $2l$ split into two semi-samples $X'$, $X''$, with empirical frequencies $
u_A'$ and $
u_A''$, define $ho_A^{(l)} = |
u_A' - 
u_A''|$ and $ho^{(l)} = \sup_{A\in S} ho_A^{(l)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Worst-case discrepancy between two empirical frequencies on independent halves of a $2l$-sample (symmetrization device).

nodes.name: Symmetrization lemma (Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: For $l > 2/\epsilon^2$, $P\{\rho^{(l)} > \epsilon/2\} \ge \tfrac{1}{2} P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Probability that the two-sample deviation exceeds $\epsilon/2$ is at least half of the probability that the one-sample deviation exceeds $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Use Fubini on $X^{(2l)} = X'^{(l)} \times X''^{(l)}$, restrict the outer integral to the event $Q = \{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\}$, and bound the inner integral by Chebyshev applied to the binomial distribution.

nodes.name: Apply Fubini to the double-sample probability
nodes.statement: Write $P(C) = \int_{X'^{(l)}} \int_{X''^{(l)}} \theta(\rho^{(l)} - \epsilon/2) \, dP'' \, dP'$ and restrict the outer integral to the event $Q$.

nodes.name: Identify a witness event $A_0$ on each $X'\in Q$
nodes.statement:
On each fixed semi-sample $X'\in Q$, choose $A_0 \in S$ with $|
u'_{A_0} - P_{A_0}| > \epsilon$. Then $|
u'_{A_0} - 
u''_{A_0}| > \epsilon/2$ holds whenever $|
u''_{A_0} - P_{A_0}| \le \epsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Bound the inner integral by Chebyshev for the binomial
nodes.statement: $P\{|\nu''_{A_0} - P_{A_0}| > \epsilon/2\} \le 4/(\epsilon^2 l)$, so for $l \ge 2/\epsilon^2$ the inner integral is $\ge 1/2$. Substituting yields $P(C) \ge \tfrac{1}{2} P(Q)$.

nodes.name: Distribution-free uniform convergence bound (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: For $l \ge 2/\epsilon^2$, $P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\} \le 4 m^S(2l) e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Distribution-free exponential bound on the uniform deviation, with constant depending only on the growth function.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Symmetrize via Lemma 2; average $\rho^{(l)}$ over all permutations $T$ of the $2l$-sample (using exchangeability of $P$); reduce the supremum to a max over essentially distinct subsamples (count $\le \Delta^S \le m^S(2l)$); bound each tail by the hypergeometric estimate $\Gamma \le 2 e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8}$.

nodes.name: Reduce one-sample to two-sample deviation via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2, $P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\} \le 2 P\{\rho^{(l)} > \epsilon/2\}$, so it suffices to bound the latter.

nodes.name: Symmetrize via permutations and reduce to essentially distinct subsamples
nodes.statement: Average $\theta(\rho^{(l)} - \epsilon/2)$ over all $(2l)!$ permutations $T$ of the $2l$-sample. Sets inducing the same subsample on $X_{2l}$ give the same $\rho_A$, so the supremum over $S$ reduces to a sum over the $\Delta^{S'}(X_{2l}) \le m^S(2l)$ essentially distinct subsamples.

nodes.name: Bound the per-event hypergeometric tail
nodes.statement: For fixed $A$, the average over permutations equals the urn-type quantity $\Gamma = \sum_{k:|2k/l - m/l| \ge \epsilon/2} \binom{m}{k}\binom{2l-m}{l-k}/\binom{2l}{l}$, which satisfies $\Gamma \le 2 e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8}$ (proof omitted in the paper).

nodes.name: Combine to obtain the final bound
nodes.statement: Summing over the essentially distinct subsamples gives $P\{\rho^{(l)} > \epsilon/2\} \le 2 m^S(2l) e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8}$. Then Lemma 2 yields $P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\} \le 4 m^S(2l) e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8}$.

nodes.name: Polynomial growth implies uniform convergence (Corollary to Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: If there exists a finite $n$ with $m^S(l) \le l^n + 1$ for all $l$, then relative frequencies converge uniformly (in probability) to probabilities over $S$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial growth function implies uniform convergence in probability.
assumptions: Exists finite $n$ with $m^S(l) \le l^n + 1$ for all $l$

nodes.name: Almost-sure uniform convergence (Theorem 3)
nodes.statement: If $m^S(l) \le l^n + 1$, then $P\{\pi^{(l)} \to 0\} = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial growth function implies almost-sure uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Use Theorem 2 to bound $P\{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\} \le 4(2l)^n e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8} + O(1)$, summable in $l$. Apply the Borel-Cantelli-type lemma cited in the paper to conclude almost-sure convergence.

nodes.name: Glivenko's theorem
nodes.statement: For $X = \mathbb{R}$ and $S = \{(-\infty, a] : a\in\mathbb{R}\}$, $m^S(l) = l + 1$, hence by Theorem 3, $P\{\sup_a |F_l(a) - F(a)| \to 0\} = 1$, recovering the Glivenko-Cantelli theorem.
nodes.statement_clean: Glivenko's theorem on uniform convergence of empirical CDFs is a special case of Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Sample-size estimate
nodes.statement: For $m^S(l) \le l^n + 1$, the inequality $4 m^S(2l) e^{-\epsilon^2 l / 8} \le \eta$ holds when $l \ge \frac{16}{\epsilon^2}\bigl(n \log(2l) + \log(4/\eta)\bigr)$ (form recovered from the source).
nodes.statement_clean: Explicit sufficient sample size for $\epsilon, \eta$-uniform convergence under polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Subadditivity of the index logarithm
nodes.statement: $\log_2 \Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_{l_1+l_2}) \le \log_2 \Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_{l_1}) + \log_2 \Delta^S(x_{l_1+1},\dots,x_{l_1+l_2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: The log-index is subadditive across sample concatenation.

nodes.name: Existence of entropy rate (Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: The sequence $H^S(l)/l$ has a limit $c \in [0,1]$ as $l \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-sample normalized entropy converges (subadditive sequence).

nodes.name: Concentration of normalized log-index (Lemma 4)
nodes.statement: $\lim_{l\to\infty} P\bigl( |l^{-1} \log_2 \Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_l) - c| > \epsilon \bigr) = 0$ for every $\epsilon > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalized log-index concentrates in probability around the entropy rate $c$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Split into one-sided tail probabilities $P^+$ and $P^-$. For $l = n l_0$ exploit subadditivity to write $l^{-1}\log_2 \Delta^S$ as an average of i.i.d. copies of $l_0^{-1}\log_2 \Delta^S$ on disjoint blocks; apply Chebyshev. For general $l$, sandwich between consecutive multiples of $l_0$. The lower-tail $P^-$ is handled by an integration argument using $E[\bullet] = H^S(l)/l$.

nodes.name: Necessary and sufficient condition for uniform convergence (Theorem 4)
nodes.statement: The relative frequencies converge (in probability) to probabilities uniformly over $S$ if and only if $\lim_{l\to\infty} H^S(l)/l = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Vanishing entropy rate is necessary and sufficient for distribution-dependent uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: Sufficiency: split the symmetrization integral by whether $\log_2 \Delta^S(x_{2l}) \le 2\delta l$ (use the bound from Section 1.4) or not (use Lemma 4 for the tail). Necessity: assume $c > 0$; pick $q$ with $q\log_2(2e/q) < c$; show via Lemma 1 that with high probability $S$ shatters a fraction-$q$ subsample; use the urn estimate and Chebyshev to lower-bound $P\{\rho^{(l)} > 2\epsilon\}$.

nodes.name: Sufficiency: split integral by entropy event
nodes.statement: Set $\delta = \epsilon^2/16$ and split $X^{(2l)}$ into $X^{(2l)}_1 = \{\log_2 \Delta^S(x_{2l}) \le 2\delta l\}$ and its complement. On $X^{(2l)}_1$ bound the symmetrized integrand by $2(2/e)^{2\delta l + 1}/8$; on the complement use $P^+(2l, \delta) \to 0$ from Lemma 4.

nodes.name: Sufficiency: conclude via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Combine to obtain $P(C) \le 2(2/e)^{2\delta l + 1}/8 + P^+(2l,\delta) \to 0$, hence $P(Q) = P\{\pi^{(l)}>\epsilon\} \to 0$ by Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Necessity: reduce $P(Q)$ to two-sample event $C'$
nodes.statement: Define $C' = \{\sup_{A\in S} |\nu'_A - \nu''_A| > 2\epsilon\}$. Independence of the semi-samples gives $P(C') \le 2 P(Q) - P^2(Q)$, hence $P(Q) \ge \tfrac{1}{2} P(C')$.

nodes.name: Necessity: pick $q$ with $q\log_2(2e/q) < c$ and find shattered fraction-$q$ subsample
nodes.statement: Choose $0 < q < 1/4$ small enough that $q \log_2(2e/q) < c$. By Lemma 4 and Lemma 1, $P\{\Delta^S(x_1,\dots,x_l) \ge \Phi([ql], l)\} \to 1$, so with high probability $S$ shatters a subsample of size $[ql]$.

nodes.name: Necessity: lower-bound $P(C')$ via urn estimate
nodes.statement: Group permutations of the $2l$-sample by partition into halves; on each shattered $[ql]$-subsample, use a hypergeometric-tail Chebyshev bound to show that the inner integrand $Z$ satisfies $Z \ge (1 - 1/(l\epsilon^2))$ for $l > 1/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Necessity: conclude $\lim P(C') = 1$
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates yields $\lim_{l\to\infty} P(C') \ge \lim_{l\to\infty} P(B) = 1$ where $B$ is the event of (24). Hence $\lim_l P\{\sup_A |\nu_A - P_A| > \epsilon\} = 1$, contradicting uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Bernoulli's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: For a single event $A$, the relative frequency $\nu_A^{(l)}$ converges in probability to $P_A$ as $l \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical weak law for a single event.
nodes.origin_citation: Bernoulli; cf. Gnedenko, Theory of Probability

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli-style probability lemma (cited)
nodes.statement: If $\sum_l P(A_l) < \infty$ for the events $A_l = \{\pi^{(l)} > \epsilon\}$, then $P\{\pi^{(l)} \to 0\} = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard summability lemma underpinning the conversion from in-probability to almost-sure convergence.
